timing.note: peak = the highest cap the momentum sampler saw (every ~4 min per coin); a peak inside 5 min of the signal means the desk entered after the move. Peaks between samples are not seen, so 'later' is a floor and 'before' a ceiling.

reeval.lookAhead: re-evaluation reads only fields written at detection; outcomes, peaks and horizon marks are used only to score. Split by detection date, older half first. Rows written before gate evidence was recorded leave four gates unchecked, so the pass count is an upper bound until every row carries it.

samplingLimit: the record has no full price series per coin: peaks are what the ~4-minute sampler saw, so a 2x that lasted ninety seconds reads as DEAD. DOUBLED counts are a floor. A per-coin high since entry needs a faster read (RPC websocket on the pool) before the label can be trusted upward.
scope: what the logged signals did, re-read under the current rule book. Descriptive bookkeeping on one desk's record; not a forecast, not a fitted model, not evidence of edge until the expectancy card's own tests pass out of sample.

sets.name: Structure only
sets.why: the base rate: every first signal with no recorded structural objection

rules.text: mint and freeze authority not active where they were read (unread passes: the read usually lands after the first signal)
top-10 holders at most 45% where read (unread passes)
Jupiter cross-check not diverging and not no-reliable-price (unchecked, failed or unrecorded passes)

sets.name: Two-sided tape
sets.why: a buy share of 1.00 was the median for winners and losers alike; this asks for real selling being absorbed

rules.text: mint and freeze authority not active where they were read (unread passes: the read usually lands after the first signal)
top-10 holders at most 45% where read (unread passes)
Jupiter cross-check not diverging and not no-reliable-price (unchecked, failed or unrecorded passes)
at least 5 sells and 30 buys in the hour, and a 5-minute buy share between 0.55 and 0.9

sets.name: Attention
sets.why: boost, narrative hit and Bluesky mentions were the only stored features with separation in the record

rules.text: mint and freeze authority not active where they were read (unread passes: the read usually lands after the first signal)
top-10 holders at most 45% where read (unread passes)
Jupiter cross-check not diverging and not no-reliable-price (unchecked, failed or unrecorded passes)
one attention confirmation: boosted, a narrative hit, or at least 3 Bluesky mentions in the hour

sets.name: Past the first minutes
sets.why: under $100k cap the median net result was -100% and a third of coins had peaked inside 15 minutes

rules.text: mint and freeze authority not active where they were read (unread passes: the read usually lands after the first signal)
top-10 holders at most 45% where read (unread passes)
Jupiter cross-check not diverging and not no-reliable-price (unchecked, failed or unrecorded passes)
pair at least 10 minutes old at the signal
cap at the signal at least $100,000

sets.name: Combined
sets.why: all of the above except the cap floor, plus the serial-relaunch filter

rules.text: mint and freeze authority not active where they were read (unread passes: the read usually lands after the first signal)
top-10 holders at most 45% where read (unread passes)
Jupiter cross-check not diverging and not no-reliable-price (unchecked, failed or unrecorded passes)
at least 5 sells and 30 buys in the hour, and a 5-minute buy share between 0.55 and 0.9
one attention confirmation: boosted, a narrative hit, or at least 3 Bluesky mentions in the hour
pair at least 10 minutes old at the signal
the same symbol logged at most 1 time in the 24 hours before (a lower bound: only coins the desk logged count)

caveats: 5 sets are read on the same record, so the best of them is biased upward.

The sets were fixed before being run (no search over parameters), but their parameters were informed by this same record (the $100k floor and the choice of attention features come from it), so the newer half is not out-of-sample for them. The clean evidence is rows detected after 2026-11-17.

Each coin's FIRST signal is all the record keeps (median about two and a half minutes old), so a rule about a later state of the coin (age, a two-sided tape) passes few rows: that is a limit of the record, not evidence against the rule.

A win is a sampled touch of the target or of 2x; net figures sell when the row was graded, net of pool fees and impact at the liquidity recorded. Rows with no outcome are left out of n. The hold figure covers only rows with a 72 h mark (recorded since 2026-10-20) and counts a rugged pool as -100%.
Rows stored before 2026-11-17 carry the old acceleration figure and the old meaning of the graduate flag; neither is used by these rules.

For the tape, attention, age, cap and relaunch rules a row whose input was not recorded does not pass. The three structure rules block only on a recorded objection, so a row with nothing recorded passes them; each shows how many of its passes were of that kind. A failed boost or narrative read is stored as a negative, so it counts as a fail, not as unrecorded.
Under 50 priced rows a set shows counts only. No candidate is a live rule and none is a claim of edge.

notKilled.label: no hard kill at the look

leftCurve.label: off the bonding curve at the look

sameCoinsFirstSignal.label: the same coins, from their first signal

caveats: One row per coin, written on the first fresh refresh between 30 and 90 minutes after its first logged signal, whatever the coin had done by then. Time is the only trigger; no score or outcome selects the row.

Only coins the desk was still tracking get one. The tracked list is capped and drops the lowest-scored names first, so the second looks lean toward coins that still scored: this is a record of survivors of the desk's own list, not of every launch.

Each row is measured from its own cap and liquidity at the look, by the same grader as every other row: a win is a sampled touch of the target or of 2x from the look, and net figures sell when the row was graded, net of pool fees and impact.

The decision is made once, on the first fresh refresh at or after the delay. A coin with a hard kill standing is still written (the count says how many), and the 'no hard kill' line leaves those out using only what was read at the look. No row is written when the cap or pool reads missing or zero at that refresh (nothing can be measured from it), when the cap is at or above the target (no entry to measure), or when the coin was dropped from the tracked list or stopped being returned by the feed before the look. Each of the three is counted per tracked pool, so a coin with two pools can count twice. Windows that fell across a restart or a re-track are not counted. A pump.fun coin that moves to a new pool before the look is read only if the desk also tracks the new pool, so graduates are under-represented.

Second looks are open rows in the same grader queue as first signals (oldest first, a fixed number per pass), so with a backlog every open row, first signals included, is revisited somewhat less often once coins are no longer tracked.
The first-signal line covers the same coins from their earlier, lower entry, so the two lines are two entries into the same coins, not two independent samples.
Rows detected before this recording began do not exist: the second-look record starts at its first row and nothing is back-filled.
Under 50 priced rows the readout shows counts only. A second look is a recording, never a verdict, and none of this is a claim of edge.
